html:
German New Guinea was the colony Germany held from 1884 to 1914 over northeast New Guinea, the Bismarck Archipelago and Bougainville. It was run at first by the New Guinea Company and later by the state.

Germans set up coconut plantations worked by labourers recruited from across the islands, and Lutheran and Catholic missions spread along the coast. Plantation life helped make Tok Pisin the common language. The capital was moved to Rabaul in 1910.

Australian troops took the colony in September 1914. It became the Mandated Territory of New Guinea under Australia, later joined with the Territory of Papua in the south to form today's country.
